discovery_disclosure: During transition-registry inspection after the response-blind epiphyte coverage preflight, unadjusted next-year retention fractions were seen to increase across rounded epiphyte-load classes. Therefore this analysis is not response-unopened confirmatory evidence. The purpose of the frozen follow-up is to determine whether that pooled pattern survives within-transect adjustment and known physical/seasonal controls.
ecological_question: Is qualitative epiphyte burden a local leaf-scale stressor that predicts next-year Thalassia recorded-state instability, or does it mainly mark persistent mature/favorable meadow state?

measurement.point_year_aggregation: mean ordinal epiphyte score across valid focal rows at the same Transect x Site x AssessmentYear
measurement.baseline_bb: mean numeric leading Braun-Blanquet class from focal SpeciesAbundance at the same point-year
measurement.depth_m: median absolute source Depth / 100 among sampled rows at the same point-year
measurement.season: mean sine and cosine of source ObservationDate day-of-year

transition_population.unit: stable Transect x meter-mark Site x consecutive AssessmentYear transition
transition_population.source_requirement: Thalassia recorded and valid epiphyte density in source year
transition_population.target_requirement: same Transect x Site sampled in AssessmentYear + 1
transition_population.outcome: target-year Thalassia recorded retention (1) versus recorded loss (0)
transition_population.reason: pre-existing Tampa protocol/date audit marks target 2016 as anomalous; include it only as sensitivity

primary_analysis.purpose: Estimate within-transect epiphyte signal rather than pooled between-site association.
primary_analysis.within_node_centering: source epiphyte score minus mean source epiphyte score among eligible transitions for that Transect
primary_analysis.model: logit(retained_next_year) ~ epi_within_node + source_bb + source_depth_m + sin_doy + cos_doy + node_id FE + source_year FE
primary_analysis.estimator: L2-regularized logistic regression with C=1.0, lbfgs, max_iter=3000

interpretation.ci_below_zero: Within a stable transect, unusually high epiphyte burden predicts lower next-year recorded retention, consistent with a local epiphyte-stress signal.
interpretation.ci_above_zero: Within a stable transect, unusually high epiphyte burden predicts higher next-year recorded retention; reject the simple annual epiphyte-stress interpretation and treat load as a state marker / candidate mature-canopy signal at this timescale.
interpretation.ci_overlaps_zero: No robust independent year-ahead epiphyte signal after baseline state, depth, season, year and stable transect identity.

secondary_analysis.pooled_model: logit(retained_next_year) ~ epiphyte_score + source_bb + source_depth_m + sin_doy + cos_doy + water_body + source_year
secondary_analysis.purpose: Quantify how the pooled association differs from the within-transect primary coefficient; this is a scale/confounding diagnostic, not an independent primary test.
secondary_analysis.type_fields: EpiphyteType_1..3 are descriptive only and cannot be searched to rescue a null primary density effect.
secondary_analysis.sensitivity: Repeat the primary model including target 2016; conclusion changes only if sign/interval classification changes.

claim_boundary: Recorded loss is an observation-state endpoint, not demographic extinction.
EpiphyteDensity is qualitative ordinal load, not measured biomass or percent light attenuation.
A negative coefficient is consistent with epiphyte stress but does not prove shading causality.
A positive coefficient is not evidence that epiphytes benefit Thalassia; it may reflect leaf longevity, mature canopy state, grazing, hydrodynamics or favorable microsite conditions.
Because the unadjusted outcome gradient was seen before this follow-up was frozen, label all inference exploratory/post-hoc.
Do not tune epiphyte categories, type subsets, lag windows, node subsets or target years after the adjusted result is opened.
